claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured; the change never reads them. When no SurrogateType is given, CreateContractlessMembers runs unconditionally. It ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract], [DataMember] and [IgnoreDataMember] on T and serializes every public read-write member under its CLR name. As a result, a member marked [IgnoreMember] (e.g. a secret) is still serialized. Custom string keys and int keys on T are also replaced by member names, so the wire format differs from what the dynamic resolver produces for the same type. The README and attribute docs describe this always-contractless behaviour, which contradicts the requirement.

claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the first (most derived) symbol of each name and then filters with IsPublicReadWrite. If a derived class overrides only the getter (public override int X => ...), Roslyn exposes no SetMethod on the override, so X is filtered out. The base read-write X is skipped by the name check. The same happens when a derived non-public member hides a public base member. The property is then silently left out of the contractless contract.

claim: The generator hook-up in GeneratorUtilities excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the hand-written formatter registration only by matching the attribute's display name. The user-declared formatter is still registered as an ObjectSerializationInfo in the resolver. Existing users who already have a hand-written formatter with this attribute name cannot be affected, but the new `partial class` emission means the generated class declaration omits the user's accessibility, modifiers and type constraints. For an `internal sealed partial` or `public sealed` user formatter this would produce CS0262 or CS0263 conflicts, and for a formatter with its own base class the generated declaration will conflict. The generated declaration also repeats the interface list, which is allowed, but a mismatch in the sealed or static modifiers is a compile error in the user's project.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public sealed partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.T>;`, and check that the generated output compiles without CS0262/CS0263 or other modifier-conflict errors.

claim: The contractless mode differs from the real ContractlessStandardResolver. It serializes only public read-write members, skips get-only properties and readonly fields, sorts the members ordinally, and uses no constructor. It also flags the keys as string keys with the intKey index set to the sorted position. Wire bytes from this formatter would differ from `MessagePackSerializer` with ContractlessStandardResolver for the same type, for example by dropping get-only members. Users who migrate from the contractless resolver to the generated formatter would notice the difference. The ledger says to follow the requirement here, and the requirement only says 'public members', so this is an unresolved gap.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a class `T { public int A {get;set;} public int B {get;} public readonly int C; }`. Serialize an instance with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the generated formatter, then compare the bytes: the get-only B and readonly C will be missing.
